 Tallison Teixeira learned heel hooks training with Valter Walker, Shamil Gaziev ‘in trouble’ at UFC Qatar
 Valter Walker believes Tallison Teixeira can submit Shamil Gaziev in Doha
 by Guilherme Cruz Nov 20, 2026, 11:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Valter Walker and Tallison Teixeira at Gor MMA Photo via Teixeira Guilherme Cruz is a Brazilian journalist covering combat sports since 2008. Tallison Teixeira is set to take on Shamil Gaziev on Saturday’s UFC Qatar card, and the timing couldn’t have been better for the Brazilian heavyweight.
 “Xicao” flew to Germany for a seminar and decided to accept an invitation from Valter Walker to spend time training with him at Gor MMA in Moscow. The promotion called soon after that to offer a three-round fight with Gaziev for Nov. 21 in Doha, a shorter distance from Russia than Brazil or the United States, and it all made sense for him.
 Teixeira, who was stopped early by Sergei Pavlovich in his most recent bout, learned from the men who trained with and coached him up until that point, so that would be beneficial. On top of that, he learned some tricks when it comes to heel hooks by working with Walker, who has scored tap-outs in his past five UFC bouts.
 “Oh, of course. I’ve already added a few to my arsenal,” Teixeira told MMA Fighting. “I’ve added a couple of [heel hooks] to my arsenal. If he makes a mistake, I’m taking his foot home [laughs].”
 Gaziev is 4-3 under the UFC banner with six fights ending by knockout, but the 6-foot-7 Brazilian wouldn’t be surprised if the Russian talent enters the cage looking for a more grappling-oriented game plan.
 “If he tries to take me down, that’s something I’ve been working on a lot over the past few months,” Teixeira said. “I’ve been improving my takedown defense and putting in a lot of work on it. And even if he does manage to take me down, it’s not the end of the world. He doesn’t have jiu-jitsu. The most he has is that wrestling control, but he doesn’t have jiu-jitsu. I believe I’ll be able to handle myself very well, either by scrambling out of positions, reversing the position and getting on top, or even getting back to my feet.”
 Walker will corner Teixeira at UFC Qatar and is confident his friend can get the job done on the ground—and not only via heel hook.
 “Can you imagine Xicao catching Gaziev with an arm-triangle choke? It wouldn’t be hard, man,” Walker said. “He’s already caught me in a few arm-triangle chokes during training, and let me tell you, they’re tough to deal with. I believe in him, man. His jiu-jitsu is way above average. He’s got high-level boxing, too. I’m putting everything on Xicao this Saturday.”
 Teixeira said that training in Russia has pushed him to another level of evolution since he now has bigger men to work with him in the gym, and can’t help but wonder where he would have be in his career if that was the case from the start. Teixeira is 2-2 in the UFC with wins over Justin Tafa and Tai Tuivasa, and quick knockout losses to Pavlovich and Derrick Lewis.
 “We know there’s a huge difference between exchanging power with a middleweight and with someone who fights at heavyweight,” Teixeira said. “I believe that some of my previous fights would have had different outcomes if I had already been training with bigger guys. Even Tuivasa, I wouldn’t have gotten as tired because there’s a difference between training three rounds with a smaller guy and training three rounds with someone who cuts weight to fight at heavyweight.”
 Teixeira said he’s more mature emotionally since the Pavlovich defeat, eyeing a slower build in the rankings if victorious in Qatar. Teixeira likes the idea of getting matched up against Thomas Petersen or Steven Asplund next after securing a finish over Gaziev.
 “He has a very dangerous right hand but again, what heavyweight doesn’t have a dangerous hands?” Teixeira laughed. “But I believe I have more ways to win this fight, you know? He’s a dangerous guy, but I’m very confident about this. I can either knock him out or submit him because he’s a guy who constantly comes forward and ends up exposing himself a little more, leaving more openings. He gets tired faster than I do [laughs]. I believe he’ll expose himself even more, especially because I’m bigger. He’ll have to close the distance more. He’s going to be in trouble with me.”
